translationRepairs: Fish calamity: In the third month of Liang's Datong year 10, the emperor visited Zhufang; at Sichuan and Xuanwu Lake, fish raised their heads above the water as if gazing at the imperial carriage.

Fish calamity: In the third month of Liang's Datong year 10, the emperor visited Zhufang; in the four moats and at Xuanwu Lake, the fish all raised their heads above the water as if gazing at the imperial carriage.
四塹 means 'the four moats', not the place Sichuan.
The emperor entered the palace and drowned.
After the emperor entered the palace, the fish disappeared.
沒 refers to the fish submerging/disappearing; the emperor did not drown.
In Wei Jiaoping year 4, fish had gathered on the roof of the armory.
In Wei's Jiaping year 4, fish had gathered on the roof of the armory.
嘉平 is romanized Jiaping, not Jiaoping.
At that time Prince Qin Xiaojun exploited the people and lavishly built mansions.
At that time Jun, Prince Xiao of Qin, exploited the people and lavishly built mansions.
秦孝王俊 is Jun, posthumously Prince Xiao of Qin; 'Xiaojun' is not a name.
On the guiwei day of the seventh month of Chen's Tiancheng year 6, a great wind from the southwest blew down the Spirit Terrace observation tower.
On the guiwei day of the seventh month of Chen's Tianjia year 6, a great wind from the southwest blew down the Spirit Terrace observation tower.
天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng.
In the sixth month of Northern Zhou's Jiande year 6, at Yangwu three beasts shaped like water buffalo appeared—one yellow, one red, one black.
In Northern Zhou's Jiande year 6, at Yangwu three beasts shaped like water buffalo appeared—one yellow, one red, one black.
The Chinese gives no month; 'sixth month' is not in the source.
Emperor Wucheng during Empress Dowager Ding's mourning still wore crimson robes.
Emperor Wucheng, while in mourning for the empress dowager, still wore crimson robes as before.
丁太后憂 means 'observing mourning for the empress dowager'; 丁 is not her surname.
In Northern Zhou's Baoqing year 3, a man bore a son with genitals on his back like a tail and foot toes like beast claws.
In Northern Zhou's Baoding year 3, someone bore a son with genitals on his back like a tail and toes like beast claws.
保定 is Baoding, not Baoqing.
In year 6, a maid of Li Laizhu in Zhao Commandery bore a thing as large as an egg.
In year 6, a maid in the household of Li Laiwang of Zhao Commandery bore a thing as large as an egg.
李來王 is romanized Li Laiwang.
Prince Qi Yang encountered and beheaded him.
Jian, Prince of Qi, encountered him and beheaded him.
